group_note: All six are plain_mcq: a question with four short answers, no lettered block, no list and no scheme, so E1 is the same across the group and the reader's grouping on structure=plain holds for every member. All six are also single_step, because each turns on one fact or one claim with no result carried forward. The demand axis is recall for five of them; q107 alone is concept_discrimination, and the stated difference is that its three wrong options are the definitions of three neighbouring allele relationships (complete dominance, linkage, mutual recessiveness), so the live decision is between concepts rather than retrieval of one fact. E2 splits on the options alone, not on the subject matter: q103, q104, q105 and q108 offer single names or terms (name_or_identify), while q106 and q107 offer whole claims to be graded (pick_correct_statement). Content shapes differ because the material differs, and each is paired with a concept a student could revise. Traps were written only where one option can be tied to one named mis-step. The recurring device is an option carrying a true fact about a neighbouring member of the same family: another follicle layer in q103, another allele relationship in q107, another structural polysaccharide in q108. q104 is the only negated task and therefore the only one carrying true_statement_trap, once per true character. Three options were deliberately left untagged (q105 options 2 and 4, q108 option 1) because no mis-step I could name lands on them; each is recorded in that question's note. No trap sits on an official answer, and no option carries two traps.
